title: Payment & Fraud
description: Payment, subscription, and webhook workflow integrity.

attacks.name: 3D Secure bypass
attacks.desc: If a payment callback is trusted without confirming the 3D Secure result, a challenge can be skipped.
attacks.prevention: Verify payment success and 3D Secure status with the payment provider before granting goods or access.

attacks.name: Card testing (BIN attack)
attacks.desc: Repeated low-value card authorizations can be used to test stolen payment card details.
attacks.prevention: Use provider fraud controls, velocity limits, and monitoring for repeated low-value authorizations.

attacks.name: Webhook replay
attacks.desc: Accepting the same signed webhook more than once can repeat an order, refund, or entitlement change.
attacks.prevention: Verify webhook signatures, timestamps, and event IDs, and process each event idempotently.

attacks.name: Webhook signature absent
attacks.desc: A webhook without signature verification can be forged by anyone who can reach the endpoint.
attacks.prevention: Require cryptographic webhook signature verification against a configured secret before changing payment state.

attacks.name: Idempotency key abuse
attacks.desc: Reusing an idempotency key with a changed amount can cause inconsistent transaction state if requests are not bound to their contents.

attacks.name: Amount vs line-item mismatch
attacks.desc: When a total is trusted independently of line items, changing one side can alter the amount charged or credited.

attacks.name: Partial refund keeps full access
attacks.desc: A partial refund should update entitlements when access is tied to the refunded purchase.

attacks.name: Currency rounding abuse
attacks.desc: Repeated currency conversion or rounding can accumulate an unintended monetary difference.

attacks.name: Negative line item
attacks.desc: A negative-priced line item can reduce an order total if product and price controls are weak.

attacks.name: Plan downgrade keeps perks
attacks.desc: Subscription entitlements may persist after a downgrade if plan changes are not applied consistently.

attacks.name: Trial stacking
attacks.desc: Canceling and resubscribing may grant repeated trials when eligibility is not tied to the customer.

attacks.name: Invoice manipulation
attacks.desc: Editable invoice identifiers can change which record is viewed or paid if ownership is not enforced.
